extracted.intended_audience: DoD/installation contracting officers, financial analysts, and government auditors evaluating in-house vs. contractor performance
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and comparing projected and actual costs of performing installation support functions in-house versus contracting them out, including identifying causes of cost variances and whether anticipated savings were realized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated savings by contracting out
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated savings by contracting out (presented per year and as a total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary expected benefit in the cost comparison; shown year-by-year and summed. The report compares these estimated savings to actual contract/in-house costs to determine if savings were realized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor bid used in the cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor bid used in the cost comparison (may be a 1-year bid, include reimbursable material estimates, or be negotiated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the bid or proposed contractor price used as the basis of the initial comparison. The text notes multiple issues (e.g., using a 1-year bid to project multi-year costs, bids submitted many months before start dates, bids including items like moving or reimbursable materials) that can make the comparison inaccurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate of contract costs in the cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate of contract costs used in the cost comparison (sometimes includes items not part of the function, e.g., moving).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between the estimate used in the original comparison and actual contract costs. The appendix highlights cases where estimates included additional items or were extrapolated and therefore did not match later actual contract costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract costs (actual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual contract costs for each period (what the government actually paid or the contractor charged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per year and totaled; compared against the contractor bid/estimate and in-house costs to calculate realized savings or cost increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of in-house operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of operating the function in-house (the government's estimated or actual in-house cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the comparator to contractor costs. In some cases in-house supplemental performance or phase-in costs are included; sometimes in-house costs occur for partial periods when contracts fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total costs of operating the function
rubrics_metrics.description: Total government cost of the function (sum of contract costs and any government-provided/supplemental resources or in-house costs where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects the full government cost exposure; the appendix shows totals used to judge whether contracting produced net savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost increases (decreases) from estimates/bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported cost increases or decreases (difference between estimated bid/expected cost and actual contract cost) for each year and in total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulated per year with explanations; reviewers attribute increases to specific causes to assess whether they undermine anticipated savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution: whether cost increases would have occurred in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether identified cost increases (e.g., additional work, wage increases) would have likely occurred if the function had remained in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine if cost increases actually reduce anticipated savings from contracting-out. The report repeatedly distinguishes increases that are 'likely' to have occurred in-house versus those attributable to contracting (claims, contract errors, higher subsequent bids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: additional work / increased scope / workload increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional work or an increased scope of work (workload increases, incorporation of new tasks after award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequently listed as a cause of higher contract costs; often noted that this additional work would have increased in-house costs as well and therefore may not meaningfully reduce savings attributed to contracting-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: wage increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage increases paid to contractor personnel (or resulting from market/wage changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly cited cause of cost growth; the appendix often notes that wage increases would likely have affected in-house costs as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: contractor claims against the government
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor claims (e.g., for loss of business, quantity variations, contract errors) that resulted in settlement payments to the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are repeatedly identified as a major cause of cost increases that reduce anticipated savings; these are usually attributable to contract administration or errors and not costs that would have been incurred in-house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: contract errors or ambiguities
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors or ambiguities in the contract/statement of work (underestimated scope, deficient statement of work, contract ambiguities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such problems led to higher costs, claim settlements, or negotiated adjustments; they are treated as avoidable contract administration failures that reduce anticipated savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: subsequent contract awards / subsequent contractor higher bids
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent contractors or contract extensions awarded at prices higher than the original bid used in the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher follow-on bids or contract modifications frequently increased costs beyond the original estimate. The report notes some of these increases are due to additional work while others reflect true price increases that reduce savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: reimbursable materials and expenses (including contractor travel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Increases from reimbursable materials, supplies, or contractor travel expenses added to contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items can materially raise contract costs relative to the original bid and are sometimes offset by material payment reductions elsewhere; they should be tracked separately in comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: award fees in excess of estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Award fees (e.g., cost-plus-award-fee) paid in excess of the amount estimated in the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When award fees exceed estimates, they increase government cost and reduce anticipated savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: supplemental government resources or government-furnished items
rubrics_metrics.description: Government-provided supplemental resources, deletion of government-furnished supplies/equipment, or rental of government tools/equipment to the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These augment government costs beyond contract payments; their inclusion or deletion affects the total cost calculation and the fairness of comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological issue: contract scope not specifically allocable to function (bundled contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts including multiple functions (e.g., packing, crating, and moving) where costs for the specific function can't be isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contracts bundle services and do not separately identify costs, the cost comparison may include unrelated items (e.g., moving) and distort the evaluation of contractor-versus-in-house costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological issue: failure to allocate contract modification costs to specific functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract modifications or combined installation-support contracts that do not allocate modification costs to individual functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents accurate determination of contract costs for a particular function, undermining the cost comparison's reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological issue: using bids/estimates submitted long before contract start (timing mismatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons based on contractor proposals submitted many months before actual contract start dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When bids are old relative to start date, wages, overhead, and market conditions can change, making the comparison inaccurate unless adjustments are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological issue: use of a single-year bid to estimate multi-year costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimating multi-year contract costs by extrapolating a one-year bid (e.g., using a 1-year bid for a 33-month period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extrapolation can misstate expected costs if the one-year bid doesn't account for multi-year changes (wages, scope, reimbursables).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: duty/operational interruptions or external events (e.g., power outage, loss of production)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonrecurring events (loss of production due to power outage) that reduce output or increase costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rare events should be identified and considered when attributing cost variances; they may not reflect systematic contracting deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: government claims for loss of materials, equipment repairs, and deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Government incurs costs for loss of materials, repairs, and deficiencies discovered after award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These increase net government cost and are considered when computing total operating cost; identify whether attributable to contractor actions or other causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: reimbursements to contractor for equipment damaged by the government
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments or reimbursements to contractors for government-caused damage to contractor equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such reimbursements represent additional government expense that can affect whether contracting produced savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-related adjustments: payment deductions for poor performance and contractor defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Deductions from payments for poor contractor performance, contractor defaults, and costs of returning function to in-house performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance issues can reduce or increase net government costs (deductions lower cost, defaults and re-transitions raise cost). The report documents both deductions and added costs due to poor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in and transition costs (including insufficient phase-in, facilities/equipment shortcomings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs or adjustments resulting from insufficient phase-in periods or failures to furnish acceptable facilities/equipment at conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase-in deficiencies can lead to contract adjustments or government costs (e.g., payments to offset poor phase-in). These costs should be included when judging net savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion criterion: determining whether contracting out realized savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Final assessment of whether savings were realized after accounting for actual contract costs, cost increases, and causes (with consideration of which increases would have occurred in-house).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report uses the tabulated data and cause attribution to state whether 'savings were realized by contracting this function' or 'savings were not realized.' This determination requires careful attribution and consideration of methodological limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification limitation: inability to precisely quantify how much increases are attributable to contracting
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting when reviewers 'could not quantify' the amount of cost increase solely attributable to higher prices, additional work, or other factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the report cannot allocate increases precisely among causes, it flags uncertainty and refrains from definitive conclusions about eliminated savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of added workload from outside sources (e.g., added VA linen service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounting for workload added to a contract after the original comparison (e.g., additional customers or tasks not present at time of initial cost comparison).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added workload increases contract costs and should be distinguished from price increases; when new workload did not exist during the comparison, it should not be used to conclude contracting failed unless adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of government administrative/transition costs and poor contractor performance increasing government costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that contractor poor performance and the transition to contracting sometimes increased government administrative or oversight costs (e.g., increased Air Force costs during initial contract).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include transition and oversight costs when computing net benefits; the report cites instances where such costs more than offset anticipated savings.
